title: p0106
universal_lens: The collision line is modeled as a dualistic boundary layer governed by geometric wedge constraints and attentional singularities. The defensive 'stand-in/charge-out' operator forms an exact spatial inversion of the offensive wedge, creating a zero-sum topological game where initial postural potential energy dictates the kinetic breakthrough.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats the lineman's visual focus as a Bayesian filter minimizing reaction latency to the ball's displacement. We map the 'wedge advance' to conformal prediction sets, ensuring the collective offensive push maintains structural integrity under stochastic defensive perturbations, quantifying the probability of a successful gap creation.
gse_mapping: GSE formalizes the engagement as a state-transition automaton: from static low-center-of-gravity equilibrium (wrestler stance) to dynamic charge. The engine evaluates real-time situational vectors, calculating optimal force application angles to exploit the opposing line's opening, strictly adhering to the chosen attentional trigger.

primitives.name: Attentional Trigger Selection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: In either case the line man must choose the object to be watched and concentrate upon it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: O: Attentional target (dimensionless categorical variable), C: Concentration intensity (0..1 normalized scalar)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes cognitive bandwidth is finite; tracking multiple fast-moving objects simultaneously leads to signal degradation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when O becomes ambiguous or changes faster than human saccadic limits, causing false starts or delayed reactions.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's Kalman filtering for ball trajectory prediction and GSE's event-triggered state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Reaction time variance relative to snap motion.

primitives.name: Defensive Charge Duality Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: DEFENSE The principle of defensive line work is to stand well in and to charge out, thus spreading and opening the offensive line.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P_in: Initial compact position vector (meters), V_out: Outward charge velocity vector (m/s), S: Offensive spread metric (meters)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes conservation of momentum during the initial explosive phase; assumes the offensive line reacts passively to the initial outward force.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if P_in is too shallow, resulting in insufficient leverage, or if V_out exceeds traction limits against turf friction.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's force-dispersion algorithms; mathematically represents a negative gradient descent on the offensive line's cohesion.
layer2.telemetry: Displacement of the offensive center at T+0.5s.

primitives.name: Offensive Wedge Topology Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: The line should make a wedge-shaped advance, keeping a close line.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: W: Wedge angle (radians), D: Inter-player distance constraint (meters), v_advance: Collective forward velocity (m/s)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rigid body dynamics for the collective line; assumes uniform mass distribution across the wedge front.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Topological collapse occurs if D exceeds the maximum allowable gap, allowing defensive penetration and breaking the wedge geometry.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSI's conformal coverage models, treating the offensive line as a moving convex hull pushing against a resisting field.
layer2.telemetry: Variance in inter-lineman spacing during the first two seconds of play.

These two primitives form a perfect duality: one seeks to maximize entropy (spread), while the other enforces order (close line).

The analogy to wrestling and fighting (Quote 9) grounds these abstractions in biomechanical reality. The 'low weight and tail' (Quote 12) establishes a stable potential energy well, minimizing the moment of inertia before the explosive transition to kinetic energy. The failure modes are clearly delineated: if the attentional trigger is missed, the entire geometric construction collapses into random noise. If the wedge loses its close-line constraint, the offensive pressure dissipates, allowing the defensive charge to succeed. Thus, the primitive logic relies entirely on the precise synchronization of cognitive focus and rigid geometric adherence.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the opposing agents requires recognizing that both offensive and defensive linemen are executing identical cognitive subroutines under inverted geometric constraints. Each agent must predict the opponent's trigger selection while simultaneously committing to their own. The defensive lineman anticipates the wedge formation and attempts to disrupt its cohesion via the outward charge. The offensive lineman anticipates the charge and uses the wedge topology to absorb and redirect the incoming momentum. This creates a recursive game-theoretic loop where success depends not just on raw power, but on out-thinking the opponent's geometric adaptation.

Furthermore, leakage between layers occurs if a lineman focuses on the wrong object (violating Quote 5); this cognitive leakage instantly breaks the rigid wedge or charge topology.
